tools.name: ComplianceTracker
tools.description:
Tool to retrieve, analyze, and contextualize Pillar two OECD GloBE administration rule data by jurisdiction.

**Purpose:**
• Centralize structured access to country-level Pillar 2 OECD GloBE administration rules, including legislation, status, effective dates and different groups and sub groups.
• Provide both high-level contextual insight (via the context_data action) and detailed, filterable datasets (via detail_data) to support analytics, comparisons, and downstream automation.
• Enable Xatbot and related systems to interpret, validate, filter, and paginate GloBE administration-rule information efficiently.

**Core Capabilities:**
• Surface compact contextual mappings across Country, Group, SubGroup, Legislation, Notes, and EffectiveDate using the lightweight context_data action.
• Retrieve detailed administration-rule records using detail_data, with optional complex filtering and pagination.
• Expose structured attributes covering legislation status, registration requirements, filing obligations (information returns, tax returns, domestic minimum tax), agent requirements, payment rules, transitional elections, and top-up tax form requirements.
• Provide machine-consumable outputs suitable for comparison, rule tracking, reasoning, and analytics.

**Data Domains Covered:**
• **Registration Requirements** – including registration obligations for GIR, Domestic Minimum Tax (DMT), exemptions, designated local entity permissions.
• **Information-Return Filing (GIR/DMT)** – obligations, exclusions, double-filing relief notifications, amended return considerations, deadlines, and extension provisions.
• **Tax-Return Filing (IIR/UTPR/DMT)** – filing rules, exclusions, timelines, and extension options.
• **Other Returns** – miscellaneous filings and jurisdiction-specific requirements.
• **Payment Dates** – payment timing, deadlines, and administrative notes.
• **Agent Requirements** – whether an agent is required for filing or submission.
• **Additional Compliance Elements:**
   – Exclusion for Transitional CbCR Safe Harbor
   – GIR Information Exchange Agreements
   – Filing Frequency
   – Consolidated Return Forms
• **Transitional Reporting Election** – eligibility, requirements, and filing details.
• **Top-Up Tax Forms** – form types, submission methods, and related administrative notes.

**Input Parameters:**
• **action (required):**
   – "context_data": returns compact contextual mappings for Country, Group, SubGroup, EffectiveDate, Legislation, Notes.
   – "detail_data": returns detailed administration-rule rows, with optional filters and pagination.
• **currentActionDescription (required):** a short, human-friendly text shown in the UI while the tool is executing; it must not contain instructions or influence tool behavior.
• **fields (required):** list of one or more of the supported field names
• **filters (optional for detail_data):** field-level constraints; each properties corresponds to a field and contains an array of allowed values.
• **top / skip (optional for detail_data):** pagination controls.

**Ideal Use Cases:**
• Obtain a quick relational understanding of countries, administrative groups, subgroups, and effective dates using context_data.
• Retrieve detailed rule records filtered by jurisdiction, group, subgroup, status.
• Compare administrative attributes across countries.
• Build analytics, monitoring triggers, or rule-change tracking workflows using paginated detail_data output.

**Output:**
• For **context_data**: lightweight, structured lists of unique field values supporting fast contextual reasoning.
• For **detail_data**: full administration-rule rows, filtered and paginated according to input parameters.

**Recommendation:**
• Use context_data to gather unique permissible values before constructing filters or detailed queries.
• Use detail_data for record-level retrieval and apply targeted filters to reduce response size.
• For large result sets, use pagination via 'top' and 'skip' fields.
• Pagination strategy:
   – First call: top=100, skip=0
   – Next call: top=100, skip=100
   – Continue incrementing skip by top until fewer than 'top' rows are returned.

top.description: Max rows to return (applies only to detail_data).

skip.description: Rows to skip for pagination (applies only to detail_data).

action.description: Type of operation to perform. Supported values: • context_data – return compact contextual dataset. • detail_data – return detailed rows based on 'fields', 'filters', 'top', 'skip'.

fields.description: List of fields to return when action = detail_data.

filters.description: Filters applied by field name. when action = detail_data.

Human-friendly text to show in UI. Must not affect logic or contain instructions. Required for all actions.Example: "Reading Compliance summary",
"Reading information for this [countryName]"

tools.name: FilingManagerMCPTool
tools.description:
Retrieve, filter, and search Filing Manager forms (Library + My Forms). This tool can answer direct questions about any form's metadata, including tax year end, filing deadline, form status, created date, entity information, jurisdiction, version, publication date, and more.

**What This Tool Returns:**
• Form metadata (FormId, Title, Country, Version, Status, Dates, Tax Year End, Filing Deadline)
• Library forms (published templates)
• My Forms (user-created instances which are user using)
• Supports searching and filtering forms by any metadata

**Supported Questions Examples:**
• "What is the tax year end for form 0077?"
• "When is the filing deadline for my form 0021?"
• "Show form 0044 details"
• "List Japan forms in the library"
• "Give me form 0002 metadata"

**Parameters:**
• action: library or my-forms
• startIndex/endIndex: pagination
• sortField/isAscending: sorting
• filters: filter forms by any metadata field

**CRITICAL - Data Analysis and Counting Instructions:**
• COUNT CAREFULLY: Parse the entire JSON array and count each item systematically
• VERIFY ALL MATH: Every breakdown, subtotal, percentage, and total must be mathematically correct
• CHECK COMPLETENESS: Ensure all forms are accounted for - no forms should be missing from your analysis
• VALIDATE TOTALS: When grouping by country, form type, or status, verify subtotals sum to the total count
• AVOID ASSUMPTIONS: Don't estimate or approximate - count actual data from the JSON response
• GROUP SYSTEMATICALLY: Use proper data grouping (Country → Form Type → Individual Forms)
• CALCULATE PERCENTAGES: Show distribution percentages and verify they add up to 100%
• PRESENT CLEARLY: Use structured tables or hierarchical lists for multi-dimensional breakdowns
• DOUBLE-CHECK: Before presenting any summary, verify your counts match the total and make logical sense

**Note:**
This tool returns form-level metadata only, not the values inside form fields.

action.description: Type of operation: • library – browse form templates. • my-forms – browse user's form instances created for fillup form.

tools.name: FXRateTool
tools.description:
A versatile financial tool for retrieving and analyzing foreign exchange (FX) rates. It supports real-time and historical data for spot, periodic, and tax-year rates across global currencies and countries. The tool facilitates currency conversions, multi-currency comparisons, and formal FX reporting for treasury, tax compliance, and financial analysis. It offers configurable views including simple/weighted averages and daily/monthly frequencies. Crucial: When presenting results, always specify whether the 'MultiplyBy' or 'DivideBy' calculation format is applied and what multiply by and divided by means in here.• MultiplyBy: Conversion is calculated as [Result = Source Amount * FX Rate]. Example: With FX Rate 1.5, 100 Source = 100 * 1.5 = 150 Target.
• DivideBy: Conversion is calculated as [Result = Source Amount * (1 / FX Rate) ]. Example: With FX Rate 0.5, 100 Source = 100 * (1/0.5) = 200 Target.

date.description: Single date for FX rate retrieval (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for SpotRate or TaxYearRate if startDate/endDate are not provided. Optional, defaults to today.

action.description:
Available actions:
• fx-rate-lookup: Retrieve FX rates by currency or country

endDate.description:
End date for FX rate retrieval (YYYY-MM-DD).
- Required for PeriodRate to specify the end of the period (optional, defaults to today if not provided).
- Optional for SpotRate or TaxYearRate (defaults to today).

rateType.description:
Type of FX rate to retrieve:
• SpotRate – FX rate for a single day (use 'date').
• PeriodRate – FX rate over a date range (use 'startDate' and 'endDate').
• TaxYearRate – one single year, or last year, tax-year FX rate (year is taken from 'date').

fxFormats.description:
The mathematical convention used to apply the exchange rate to the source currency:
• MultiplyBy: Conversion is calculated as [Result = Source Amount * FX Rate]. (The rate is the multiplier for the source currency).
• DivideBy: Conversion is calculated as [Result = Source Amount * (1 / FX Rate) ]. (The rate is the multiplier for the target currency).
Technical Note: For 'SpotRate' requests, only 'MultiplyBy' is supported.

startDate.description:
Start date for FX rate retrieval (YYYY-MM-DD).
- Required for PeriodRate to specify the start of the period (optional, defaults to today if not provided).
- Optional for SpotRate or TaxYearRate (defaults to today).

summeryRateView.description: Summary rate calculation method for aggregated FX rates

reportingCountries.description: Country codes to determine reporting currencies (e.g., 'US', 'FR'). Overrides 'ReportingCurrencyCodes' if provided.

transactionCountries.description: Country codes to determine transaction currencies (e.g., 'US', 'FR'). Overrides 'TranslationCurrencyCodes' if provided.

reportingCurrencyCodes.description: Currency codes to get the FX rate for (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR'). Optional if 'ReportingCountries' is provided.

translationCurrencyCodes.description: Currency codes to get the FX rate from (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR'). Optional if 'TransactionCountries' is provided.

tools.name: SourceVerification
tools.description:
Tool to verify and cross-reference information across retrieved source documents.

**When to use:**
• Call this tool after retrieving sources to verify that they adequately cover the user's question.
• You can call it again after searching for more sources — it will update and refine the previous verification with the new sources.

**How to call:**
• First, decompose the user's question into a list of specific information items that need verification.
• Example: If user asks 'Is Japan, Australia implemented Pillar 2? What is the status? What is the next filing date?'
  Pass itemsToVerify as:
  'Japan Pillar 2 status\nJapan implementation details\nJapan next filing date\nAustralia Pillar 2 status\nAustralia implementation details\nAustralia next filing date'

**What it does:**
• Checks which sources cover each information item
• Detects contradictions, outdated information, and coverage gaps
• Returns a structured verification report with confidence assessments and an overall verdict
• If called again, merges new findings with the previous verification result

itemsToVerify.description:
A newline-separated list of specific information items to verify from the sources. Break down the user's question into discrete facts/topics. Example: 'Japan Pillar 2 status
Japan implementation details
Japan next filing date
Australia Pillar 2 status'
